lesson.child_mission: Length fluency mixes choosing units, converting between cm and m and reading simple scale values accurately.
lesson.evidence_instructions: Save the independent response, specific revisions and both short-answer explanations; record oral evidence for speaking tasks.
lesson.extension: Apply the same method to a larger number or a new context, then compare two solution paths for accuracy.
lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Convert: 3 m; 125 cm; compare 2 m and 250 cm.

FEEDBACK
300 cm; 1 m 25 cm; 2 m < 250 cm (250 cm = 2 m 50 cm).

WATCH FOR
Forgetting that 100 cm = 1 m causes conversion errors.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Complete a 16-item length fluency set (convert, compare, choose unit). Re-work misses with a unit diagram.

Write a short reflection naming one step you corrected and why.

lesson.parent_notes:
Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: Complete a 16-item length fluency set (convert, compare, choose unit). Re-work misses with a unit diagram. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Original response on new material: 300 cm; 1 m 25 cm; 2 m < 250 cm (250 cm = 2 m 50 cm). Reasoning: I used fluency by attending to convert and explain why it matters rather than copying the worked model.

Parent: Written model 2: Common error: Forgetting that 100 cm = 1 m causes conversion errors. Correction: 300 cm; 1 m 25 cm; 2 m < 250 cm (250 cm = 2 m 50 cm). Why: the correction restores accurate use of fluency.

Parent: Likely misconception: Forgetting that 100 cm = 1 m causes conversion errors. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

Parent: Short-answer focus 1: Solve one fresh problem that uses fluency with different numbers from the worked model. Show working and name the places or values that matter.

Parent: Short-answer focus 2: Describe one likely mistake with fluency, show corrected working, and say why the correction works.

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
Set: 2 m = __ cm; 450 cm = __ m __ cm; which is longer, 180 cm or 1 m 90 cm?

TRY FIRST
Convert: 3 m; 125 cm; compare 2 m and 250 cm.

FEEDBACK
300 cm; 1 m 25 cm; 2 m < 250 cm (250 cm = 2 m 50 cm).
teach_steps.explain:
Length fluency mixes choosing units, converting between cm and m and reading simple scale values accurately.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner choose methods based on place value, quantity and accurate working, rather than guessing digits by shape alone. Keep every step justified.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the places, values or distances that carry the method. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Compare your working with the feedback: did you use the same skill and show your reasoning? If a digit or place is uncertain, identify what would have to be regrouped or counted again. One deliberate, justified revision is more useful than writing a longer answer.
teach_steps.notice: Forgetting that 100 cm = 1 m causes conversion errors. Correct the value or method, not just the appearance of the digits.
